practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following is considered the founder of the Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Qutub-ud-din Aibak founded the Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty in 1206 AD following the death of Muhammad Ghori, establishing the first independent Muslim rule in Northern India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History - Our Pasts II / Standard Medieval History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Qutub-ud-din Aibak officially ascend the throne of Delhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak assumed sovereign power in 1206 AD after the assassination of Muhammad Ghori, though he ruled primarily from Lahore rather than Delhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Archaeological Survey of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the popular honorific title given to Qutub-ud-din Aibak due to his immense generosity?
practiceQuestions.sol: Qutub-ud-din Aibak was known as 'Lakh Baksh' (giver of lakhs) due to his lavish distribution of wealth and charity to people. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval Indian History - Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous mosque in Delhi was commissioned by Qutub-ud-din Aibak?
practiceQuestions.sol: Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in Delhi was built by Qutub-ud-din Aibak starting around 1192 AD, erected on the site of a demolished Hindu-Jain temple complex. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) / NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q: Qutub-ud-din Aibak started the construction of the Qutub Minar in honor of which revered Sufi saint?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak initiated the construction of Qutub Minar in Delhi dedicated to the prominent Sufi saint Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / NCERT Fine Arts Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q: Which mosque located in Ajmer was constructed by Qutub-ud-din Aibak?
practiceQuestions.sol: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpara in Ajmer was built by Qutub-ud-din Aibak around 1199 AD, showcasing early Indo-Islamic architecture. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / NCERT Class 7 History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Qutub-ud-din Aibak meet his sudden death in 1210 AD?
opts: Died of cholera during a military campaign in Bengal
Assassinated by his nobles in the royal court
Fell accidentally from a horse while playing Chaugan (polo)
Poisoned by his ambitious son Aram Shah
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak died in 1210 AD in Lahore from injuries sustained after falling off a horse while playing Chaugan (polo/horse polo). [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval Indian History - Satish Chandra / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: Where is the tomb of Qutub-ud-din Aibak located?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak's tomb is located in Anarkali Bazar in Lahore, Pakistan, reflecting his administrative capital. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / Historical Gazetteers]

practiceQuestions.q: Who succeeded Qutub-ud-din Aibak briefly to the throne of Lahore/Delhi before Iltutmish?
practiceQuestions.sol: Following Aibak's sudden death, his son Aram Shah was proclaimed ruler in Lahore, but he was inefficient and soon overthrown by Iltutmish. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Medieval Historiography]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous Persian author and historian patronized by Qutub-ud-din Aibak wrote 'Taj-ul-Ma'asir'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hasan Nizami was a noted chronicler at Aibak's court who wrote 'Taj-ul-Ma'asir', an important primary source for the early Delhi Sultanate. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India / Medieval Historiography]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Qutub-ud-din Aibak operate his government primarily from Lahore rather than Delhi during his reign?
opts: Delhi lacked sufficient water resources for his large imperial army.
Lahore was strategically closer to Ghazni and provided a buffer against rival ambitious generals like Taj-ud-din Yildiz.
Delhi was severely devastated by earthquakes, forcing him to shift capital temporarily.
The local Hindu chiefs of Delhi launched constant revolts preventing any permanent settlement.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak made Lahore his capital because it was strategically vital to check the ambitions of Taj-ud-din Yildiz (ruler of Ghazni) who laid claim to Ghori's Indian conquests. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India: From Sultanate to the Mughals / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Qutub-ud-din Aibak legally structure his sovereignty vis-a-vis the successor of Muhammad Ghori?
opts: He immediately declared complete independence and minted coins in his own name without any outside reference.
He ruled without any royal titles or formal recognition, remaining a humble soldier.
He refrained from assuming the full title of Sultan, ruling initially as a Malik and Sepahsalar until Giyas-ud-din Mahmud manumitted him.
He submitted annual tributes directly to the Caliph of Baghdad, bypassing the Ghaznavid state entirely.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak did not initially assume the title of Sultan. He ruled with the title of Malik and Sepahsalar. It was only later that Ghori's successor, Giyas-ud-din Mahmud, officially manumitted him and recognized his sovereign status. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India / Delhi Sultanate Administration]

practiceQuestions.q: Which statement best describes the nature of administration established by Qutub-ud-din Aibak in the newly conquered territories?
opts: A decentralized feudal system based purely on local autonomous Hindu kings without Islamic legal interference.
A military-dominated governance relying heavily on trusted Turkish slave officers (Iqtadars/commanders) to maintain order and collect revenue.
A democratic tribal assembly system modeled after Central Asian nomadic councils (Kurultai).
A rigid bureaucratic civil service chosen through open competitive examinations similar to the Chinese exam system.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak's administrative mechanism relied heavily on military commanders and trusted Turkish slave-officers stationed across strategic outposts to extract tribute and suppress local rebellions, forming the precursor to the Iqta system. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra / NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Qutub-ud-din Aibak's matrimonial alliances in consolidating his power?
opts: He married the daughter of Prithviraj Chauhan to placate the Rajput nobility.
He secured his flanks by marrying his sister to Taj-ud-din Yildiz and giving his own daughter in marriage to Shams-ud-din Iltutmish.
He forged an alliance with the Khwarizm Shah by marrying a princess of Transoxiana.
He avoided all matrimonial alliances to prevent internal factionalism among Turkish officers.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak used smart matrimonial diplomacy: he married Yildiz's sister, gave his daughter to Iltutmish (then a rising commander), and cemented ties with Nasir-ud-din Qabacha by marrying another daughter to him. [Primary Reference: Medieval Indian History Textbooks / Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of early Indo-Islamic architecture, what structural technique characterized the buildings constructed during Aibak's era (like Quwwat-ul-Islam)?
opts: True voussoir arches and domes built with complete lime-mortar masonry from scratch.
Trabeate (corbelled) construction principles adapted by reusing columns and materials from destroyed indigenous temples.
Monolithic rock-cut excavation techniques similar to Ellora caves.
Pre-stressed concrete skeletal frameworks introduced from Central Asia.
practiceQuestions.sol: Early monuments built under Aibak, such as the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Adhai Din Ka Jhonpara, primarily used the trabeate system (lintel and beam) by repurposing carved pillars from destroyed Hindu and Jain temples. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Fine Arts - An Introduction to Indian Art / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is Qutub-ud-din Aibak's reign historically categorized as the foundational phase rather than the consolidation phase of the Delhi Sultanate?
opts: Because he ruled for only about four years and spent most of his energy fending off external Turkish rivals and keeping territories together without institutionalizing systemic revenue reforms.
Because he was a puppet ruler controlled entirely by Hindu vassals in Northern India.
Because he rejected Islam and tried to synthesize a new syncretic religion.
Because he transferred all authority back to the Ghaznavid Empire before his death.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak's brief tenure (1206-1210 AD) was marked by the mere survival and initial planting of Turkish rule. True institutional consolidation (like the Iqta system, Turkan-i-Chahalgani, and currency reforms) was carried out later by his successor, Iltutmish. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra / Bipan Chandra History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Qutub-ud-din Aibak manage relations with neighboring regional powers like the Rajputs and local Indian rulers?
opts: Through total annihilation and conversion of the entire local population.
Through a mix of aggressive military raids to subdue strongholds, followed by occasional compromises and tributary extraction when direct control was unfeasible.
By granting complete sovereignty and tax exemptions to all Rajput kingdoms.
By entering into a confederacy against Central Asian invaders.
Through peaceful missionary activities and trade agreements.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak conducted extensive military campaigns across northern India (including Kalinjar, Gwalior, and Gujarat), but due to the fluid political situation, many regional chiefs accepted nominal suzerainty and paid tribute rather than facing complete permanent annexation. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Standard Medieval Chronicles]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the socio-political status of Mamluks (slaves) like Qutub-ud-din Aibak within the military-aristocratic hierarchy of the 13th-century Islamic world?
opts: They were treated as deprived serfs with no civil or military rights.
They were elite military slaves trained in governance and martial arts who often enjoyed high trust, loyalty bonds, and paths to ultimate political power.
They were religious clerics who oversaw Islamic jurisprudence.
They were foreign mercenaries hired temporarily without any integration into the ruling elite.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mamluk system inverted traditional notions of slavery; military slaves were trained, educated, and heavily relied upon by masters like Ghori, often rising to occupy high commands and sovereign states based on personal capability and loyalty. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Cambridge Economic History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Qutub-ud-din Aibak's governance impact the religious and cultural landscape of urban centers in northern India?
opts: It resulted in complete destruction of all urban trading networks and total ruralization of the economy.
It marked the introduction of Islamic architectural elements, mosques, and Sufi institutional focal points in key cities like Delhi and Ajmer.
It fostered the revival of Vedic temple building and Sanskrit literature patronage.
It isolated Indian urban centers from Central Asian trade routes completely.
practiceQuestions.sol: Aibak's construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Adhai Din Ka Jhonpara symbolized the institutionalization of Muslim political presence and the inception of Indo-Islamic synthesis in urban nodes. [Primary Reference: NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art / ASI]

practiceQuestions.q: In assessing the military career of Qutub-ud-din Aibak under Muhammad Ghori prior to 1206 AD, what was his primary role?
opts: Chief naval commander securing the western coastline of India.
Viceroy and chief general managing Ghori's Indian conquests, leading campaigns in Delhi, Ajmer, and the Gangetic plains.
Diplomatic envoy negotiating peace treaties with the Ghaznavid court.
Treasurer in charge of collecting international trade tariffs.
practiceQuestions.sol: Before becoming Sultan in 1206, Aibak was appointed by Muhammad Ghori as the viceroy of his Indian territories following the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), spearheading expansion into northern and eastern India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. He was originally a Turkic slave purchased by Qazi Fakhr-ud-din Abdul Aziz of Nishapur.
2. He assumed the sovereign title of 'Sultan' immediately upon the death of Muhammad Ghori in 1206 AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak was a Turkic boy sold into slavery to Qazi Fakhr-ud-din in Nishapur, from whom Muhammad Ghori eventually purchased him. Statement 2 is incorrect because Aibak did not immediately take the full title of Sultan; he initially ruled with the title of Malik and Sepahsalar, receiving formal royal manumission and recognition later from Giyas-ud-din Mahmud. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Minhaj-us-Siraj]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following architectural works:
1. Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque (Delhi)
2. Adhai Din Ka Jhonpara (Ajmer)
3. Alai Darwaza (Delhi)
Which of the above architectural monuments were commissioned/started during the reign of Qutub-ud-din Aibak?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Quwwat-ul-Islam and Adhai Din Ka Jhonpara were commissioned by Qutub-ud-din Aibak. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Alai Darwaza was constructed much later by Ala-ud-din Khilji in 1311 AD as an extension of the Qutub complex. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / NCERT Fine Arts Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military rivals and contemporaries of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. Taj-ud-din Yildiz ruled over Ghazni and posed a constant threat to Aibak's northern frontiers.
2. Nasir-ud-din Qabacha controlled Sindh and Multan, often contesting influence over Punjab.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Following Ghori's death, his empire fragmented among his leading Turkish slaves. Taj-ud-din Yildiz took Ghazni and claimed supremacy over Indian territories, while Nasir-ud-din Qabacha established himself in Sindh and Multan, making Aibak's western and northern borders heavily contested. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT Class 7 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the literary and cultural patronage of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. He patronized scholars like Hasan Nizami, author of 'Taj-ul-Ma'asir', and Fakhr-i-Mudabbir.
2. He himself was entirely illiterate and lacked any appreciation for Persian literature or poetry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak patronized prominent Persian historians and literati like Hasan Nizami and Fakhr-i-Mudabbir (who dedicated his work 'Adab-ul-Harb' to Aibak). Statement 2 is incorrect; although he was known as 'Qurankhani' for his melodious Quran recitation, he was well-read in Islamic theology and supported literary figures, contrary to the claim that he lacked appreciation for literature. [Primary Reference: Medieval Historiography / Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the origin and early life of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. He belonged to the Aibak tribe of Turkestan and was brought as a slave to Nishapur in his childhood.
2. He had a prominent physical deformity—a broken little finger—due to which he was historically known as Aibak-i-Chulak.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak belonged to the Turkestan Aibak tribe and was sold into slavery. Statement 2 is also historically documented; due to an injury or physical flaw (a broken/malformed little finger), he earned the nickname 'Aibak-i-Chulak' (the maimed Aibak). [Primary Reference: Minhaj-us-Siraj, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri / Standard Medieval Chronicles]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration and military expansion of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. He successfully annexed Bihar and Bengal by personally leading lengthy military campaigns in the east.
2. He maintained diplomatic stability by avoiding open conflicts with the Rajput states of western India throughout his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because Bihar and Bengal were brought into the sphere of influence primarily by his general Bakhtiyar Khalji, not by Aibak's personal eastern campaigns. Statement 2 is wrong because Aibak did not avoid conflicts with Rajputs; rather, he fought extensive wars against them in Kalinjar, Gwalior, and Gujarat. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the succession and death of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. Aibak died in 1210 AD in Lahore as a result of a fatal accident while playing Polo (Chaugan).
2. Following his death, the Turkish Amirs of Delhi immediately invited Shams-ud-din Iltutmish to bypass Aram Shah and take the throne.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak died in 1210 AD in Lahore after falling from his horse while playing Chaugan (polo). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Amirs of Lahore initially installed Aibak's weak son, Aram Shah. It was the Delhi Amirs who subsequently invited Iltutmish from Badaun to overthrow Aram Shah and take control. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the coins and currency system under Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. He issued gold and silver coins bearing his own name as an independent sovereign Sultan of Delhi.
2. The systematic introduction of standard silver tanka and copper jital in the Delhi Sultanate is credited to his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Aibak did not issue regular coinage in his own name as an independent Sultan with full sovereign titles since he operated largely as a Malik/deputy of Ghori's state for most of his rule. The introduction of the standard silver tanka and copper jital is universally credited to his successor, Shams-ud-din Iltutmish. [Primary Reference: Numismatic Society of India / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional foundations laid during Qutub-ud-din Aibak's reign:
1. He successfully established the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (Corps of Forty) to balance the power of regional governors.
2. He initiated the construction of the Qutub Minar, naming it after the Sufi saint Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (Corps of Forty elite Turkish slaves) was created and institutionalized later by Iltutmish, not Aibak. Statement 2 is correct: Aibak started building the Qutub Minar in Delhi, dedicating it to the revered Chishti saint Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Archaeological Survey of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding historical assessments of Qutub-ud-din Aibak:
1. Medieval chroniclers like Minhaj-us-Siraj praised him for his extreme generosity, earning him the title of 'Lakh Baksh'.
2. Modern historians view his reign as a fragile military occupation that successfully laid the geopolitical bedrock for the permanent establishment of the Delhi Sultanate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Minhaj-us-Siraj and other contemporary Persian chroniclers praised Aibak's unmatched benevolence and generosity ('Lakh Baksh'). Modern historical consensus regards his brief rule as the critical bridging phase that transitioned Ghori's conquests into an independent sovereign Delhi Sultanate under subsequent rulers. [Primary Reference: Minhaj-us-Siraj, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri / Satish Chandra Medieval India]
